item.title: MCP Server Config File Locations: Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Cursor, VS Code, Hermes, OpenClaw (2026)
item.description:
Each AI client keeps its MCP server list in its own file. This page lists the file for seven clients, the top-level key inside it, and where the file sits. Each row comes from that client’s own documentation, read on 2026-11-25. Where a client’s docs give no path for an OS, the table says so.

Where each client keeps its MCP servers

Client File Top-level key Path
Claude Code .mcp.json (project, shared) and ~/.claude.json (user and local) mcpServers .mcp.json at the project root. ~/.claude.json in your home folder. The docs give no separate Windows path.
Claude Desktop claude_desktop_config.json mcpServers macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json. Windows: %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json. Linux: ~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json.
Codex config.toml [mcp_servers.<name>] tables ~/.codex/config.toml. Per project: .codex/config.toml, trusted projects only. The docs give no Windows path.
Cursor mcp.json mcpServers Global: ~/.cursor/mcp.json. Per project: .cursor/mcp.json in the project folder.
VS Code .vscode/mcp.json (workspace) servers The workspace file is .vscode/mcp.json in the project folder. VS Code’s docs say new Copilot setups use other files: ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json (top key mcpServers) or a workspace-root .mcp.json.
Hermes Agent config.yaml mcp_servers ~/.hermes/config.yaml. The docs give no Windows path.
OpenClaw openclaw.json mcp.servers ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json. The openclaw mcp commands read and write this section.

Sources: Claude Code MCP docs (scopes: local, project, user); Claude Desktop local MCP servers, Model Context Protocol docs (the three OS paths; the VS Code configuration reference repeats them); Codex MCP docs; Cursor MCP docs (mcp.json, STDIO fields) and the VS Code configuration reference, which lists the Cursor global and workspace paths; VS Code MCP servers and VS Code MCP configuration reference; Hermes MCP docs; OpenClaw MCP registry docs. The OpenClaw file name comes from OpenClaw’s configuration docs.

item.title: OpenClaw Config File: Main Keys and Defaults (2026)
item.description:
OpenClaw reads its settings from ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json. The file is JSON5, and every field is optional. Leave a field out and OpenClaw uses its built-in default.

This page lists the top-level sections and the keys people change most. Defaults come from OpenClaw’s configuration docs, read on 2026-11-25. The docs spread the full key list over about 20 subpages, so this page is not the full list. The reference page of the docs says the same: it points to the subpage for each area.

item.title: Hermes Agent config.yaml Reference: Main Sections and Keys (2026)
item.description:
Hermes Agent keeps its settings in ~/.hermes/config.yaml. Secrets (API keys, bot tokens) go in ~/.hermes/.env. The config file wins for every non-secret setting when both are set.

This page lists the main sections and the keys people change most. The values are the ones in Hermes’s own example file, read on 2026-11-24. The file has 28 top-level sections and many more child keys. The first table lists all 28 sections. The key table covers only the main child keys, not the full list.
